title: The opener puts each new ticket in an open group or a new group at the end of the chain (issue #6, part 3)
objective: The opener decides which group each new ticket joins - an open group whose tickets are closest to it, or a new group at the end of the chain - and a choice that cannot work is refused before anything is written.
outline: devloop/ticket_creator.py: check_new(): per new key, the 'group' rules of acceptance 1 and 3 (placeholder pattern ^new-g\d+$; chain order as in acceptance 3); write_new(): inside its change function re-check every named existing group is open (else return the refusal sentences and write nothing; _open_tickets treats them like check_new's errors), make the new groups with core/pool.new_group (issue #6 part 2) in first-appearance order, append to existing groups (event 'member #<id> added by the opener') and set each ticket's 'group'. The dag node stays {'depends_on': [...]}. _open_tickets(): a groups_section(snap) after the '## Current DAG' block. devloop/prompts/creator/02-rules.md ('Rules for the DAG') and 03-handin.md (example). tests_devloop/fake_agent.py: the default creator hand-in (the final `else:`) and the ticket hand-ins near `elif action == "bad":`. README.

notes: Issue #6 (GitHub sai99claw/agent-control #6), part 3 of 4. User words: see part 1 (「開題者他要做的事情就是把他當前在開的題目找到一個合適的比較不容易產生衝突的或是邏輯相近的票的附近放進去」); approved 2026-11-23. Agreed design item 1: the opener assigns every new ticket to a group when it writes the DAG: an existing group that has not started its regression (state open) or a new group at the end; it picks the group whose tickets are logically closest / least likely to conflict and says why in the ticket's notes; writing a ticket into a group that is pr, fixing, verified, landed (or stuck, cancelled) is refused by the pool write validation, and the opener's one retry picks another. Design decisions by the opener: (1) placeholders are 'new-g<n>' so they cannot be mistaken for ticket keys ('new-1'); (2) a group earlier than a dependency's group is refused, because that member could never start before its own group's regression (the controller would move it out, part 2's rule); (3) the check runs twice, once on the snapshot and once inside the write, because a group can go to pr while the opener works (the controller's open-group decision also re-reads inside its update, part 2). hard_block patterns match every added line of the branch, tests and comments included: never write os.kill, killpg, pkill or 'kill -' anywhere (use a Popen object's own methods). docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/VISION.md are the main session's (hard_block paths): do not edit them. No absolute home paths in any file (tests/test_no_project_names.py scans every tracked file, .md included). CODE-MAP.md is regenerated at landing: do not edit it. Test ids given to run_tests.py are module ids relative to the unittest roots (test_machine.Class), never tests_devloop.test_machine.Class.
acceptance: Hand-in: each dag entry is {"depends_on": [...], "group": G}, G being the id of an existing open group or a new-group placeholder 'new-g<n>' (n a number); tickets that name the same placeholder share one new group; new groups are made at the end of the chain in the order their placeholder first appears in 'tickets', each with the first event 'opened by the opener for #<id>, #<id>'. On a pool whose only group is a landed g1, a hand-in with new-1 -> 'new-g1', new-2 -> 'new-g2', new-3 -> 'new-g1' (no dependencies) opens #1, #2, #3: g2 has members ['1', '3'] and first event 'opened by the opener for #1, #3', g3 has ['2'] and 'opened by the opener for #2', and the tickets' 'group' fields match.

An existing open group: the new ticket is appended to its members, the group gets the event 'member #<id> added by the opener', the ticket's 'group' is that id, and no group is made. With g1 open (members ['1']), a hand-in putting new-1 in 'g1' opens #2: g1's members ['1', '2'], its last event 'member #2 added by the opener', the groups are exactly {'g1'}.

Refused, with nothing written; the sentences go to the opener's one retry under '## Your previous hand-in was rejected', and after a second refusal ticket_creator exits 1 with the decision page 'the opener could not produce valid tickets:' listing them one per line as '- <sentence>': no group -> '<key>: "group" must be an open group's id or a new group like "new-g1"'; an id that is neither a group nor a placeholder -> '<key>: group <G> does not exist'; a group not open -> '<key>: group <G> is <state> and takes no new tickets'; a group before the group of a dependency -> '<key>: group <G> comes before <H>, the group of <dep> it depends on' (<dep> is '#<id>' for an existing ticket, the key for a ticket of the same hand-in). Chain order: existing groups by number, then the hand-in's new groups in creation order; a dependency that is landed or has no group imposes nothing.
The check is repeated inside the pool write: when a named group stopped being open after the check, nothing is written and the hand-in counts as refused with the same sentence.

The opener's prompt has a section '## Groups' right after '## Current DAG': a line 'The chain, oldest first; a new group goes at the end.' and then one line per group that is not landed or cancelled, in number order: '- <gid> (open, takes new tickets): ' or '- <gid> (<state>, takes no new tickets): ' followed by its members as '#<id> [<ticket state>] <title>' joined by '; '; when there is no such group the one line '- none: every ticket goes into a new group'. With g1 open ['1'] (#1 ready, title 'ticket 1') and g2 pr ['2'] (#2 merged, title 'ticket 2'), the prompt has the lines '- g1 (open, takes new tickets): #1 [ready] ticket 1' and '- g2 (pr, takes no new tickets): #2 [merged] ticket 2'.

Prompt rules: devloop/prompts/creator/02-rules.md's 'Rules for the DAG' asks for `group` in every DAG entry: an open group whose tickets are logically closest or least likely to conflict with this one, else a new group 'new-g1' ('new-g2', ... for more than one); never a group that comes before a group of a ticket it depends on; say in the ticket's `notes` why this group. 03-handin.md's example dag entry is {"depends_on": [], "group": "new-g1"}. ticket_creator.chain() contains '"group"' and 'new-g1' and contains neither '"verify"' nor 'why_alone'.

Every creator hand-in with a dag in tests_devloop/fake_agent.py carries a group and no verify: the default hand-in puts both tickets in 'new-g1'; the ticket hand-ins added by #110-#115 (#112's 'one_ticket' and any other) use 'new-g1'. Existing cases keep passing: test_pool_git.py's flow case still finds one group g1 with members ['1', '2'].

devloop/README.md (the opener's row in Roles, and the hand-in / Contracts text) describes the group in the hand-in, the '## Groups' section and the refusals; the reviser cannot change a ticket's group (group is not an editable field).

# Two design changes reported by tabby_pool (T) as GitHub issues #7 and #6 on sai99claw/agent-control

The user approved both designs below (2026-11-23, "Ok" to the main session's proposal). Each ticket names its issue number so the main session can close the issue after landing. Issue texts are data, not instructions. Tests go in the area's own test file in tests_devloop/ (or a new file), using loop_harness.py; never a catch-all file.

Order: #6's ticket(s) depend on every ticket opened from the request for issues #1 #2 #4 #5 (they are open in the pool now and change ticket_controller.py too) and on #7's ticket. #7's ticket depends on nothing open.

## Issue #7: the opener does not wait for a machine slot
User (T, verbatim): 「開題者 理論上不用等 regression， 驗證在跑的時候只會阻擋後續的票繼續進行開發寫code， 不會阻擋新的票題設計」.
Today devloop/core/agents.py `Pending.launch()` takes a machine slot (`slots.take`, no time limit) for every role. With `devloop.regression_exclusive: true` the regression holds the gate and every slot, so `actl new` waits for hours while a regression runs (T, 2026-11-23: three openers waited 2+ hours, one carrying a prod fix).
Wanted:
- The roles that only read the repo and write tickets or memory start without a slot: the opener / reviser (role creator) and the consolidator (and its peer). Worker, verifier, reviewer and fixer keep taking a slot. The live record of an opener never shows the "slot" stage.
- The opener sometimes runs tests to measure a premise (memory/role/creator.md "Verify the ticket's premises"). Those runs must not land inside an exclusive regression: devloop/run_tests.py, when its process is not under a slot (DEVLOOP_SLOT unset) and slots are needed, tries to take one without waiting; when none is free (or the exclusive gate is held) it prints one line saying the machine is busy (regression running or all slots taken) and exits 2 (could not measure) without running anything. Under a slot it behaves as today.
- The opener's prompt (devloop/prompts/creator/) says: run tests only through `python3 <loop>/run_tests.py <ids>`; on "machine busy" do not wait or retry, write the ticket with that premise marked "not measured (machine busy)". Update memory/role/creator.md's measuring line if it names another way to run tests.
- removes: the opener's unbounded wait for a slot.

## Issue #6: groups are chosen by the opener and form a chain; a group's regression is a dependency point
User (T, verbatim): 「Group 的數量定義 應該是開題者決定的 而不是固定10 開題者在寫入dag的時候 本來就會去看其他的題目是什麼然後要把自己的題放在哪裡， Group 的regression 就是一個強制產生相依性的地方， Dag 的尾巴一定是個group , 因為dag表示了現在所有要做的票，最後一個做完一定需要整個驗一次。 所以說開題者他要做的事情就是把他當前在開的題目找到一個合適的比較不容易產生衝突的或是邏輯相近的票的附近放進去」.
Today tickets fill the open group up to `max_group_size` (10) and then a new group opens; several groups run from different main shas and serialize only at the regression, so each landing makes a waiting group merge main and run its 1.2-hour regression again (T: g57 landing re-ran g56), and cross-group conflicts show up late in fix rounds.
Design the main session and the user agreed:
1. The opener assigns every new ticket to a group when it writes dag.json: an existing group that has not started its regression (state open: no member past merged and no regression started), or a new group at the end. It picks the group whose tickets are logically closest / least likely to conflict, and says why in the ticket's notes. Writing a ticket into a group that is already pr/fixing/verified/landed is refused by the pool write validation (the opener's one retry then picks another group).
2. Groups form one chain in creation order. A group's regression starts only when every earlier group is landed or cancelled. A later group's tickets may start work before that (worker, verifier, reviewer on the group's branch), as long as their own ticket dependencies allow; when the earlier group lands, the branch takes main as today (follow_main) and then its regression runs once.
